elements.element: Customer may assign to an affiliate without consent.
elements.evidence: Revised 22.4 proviso (a) covers only "a successor in a merger, acquisition or sale of all or substantially all of Customer's assets"; no consent-free assignment to a Customer affiliate appears anywhere in the clause (the deleted $100,000,000 language was an acquirer-quality test, not an affiliate carve-out).

elements.element: Customer may assign to a successor in a merger, acquisition, or sale of substantially all assets without consent.
elements.evidence: Revised 22.4: "M&I's consent need not be obtained in connection with the assignment of this Agreement to a successor in a merger, acquisition or sale of all or substantially all of Customer's assets" (subject only to the retained Section 21.11 compliance condition).

elements.element: Vendor may not assign without Customer's consent.
elements.evidence: Retained proviso (b): "M&I may freely assign this Agreement (i) in connection with a merger, corporate reorganization or sale of all or substantially all of its assets, stock or securities, or (ii) to any entity which is a successor to the assets or the business of the M&I Data Services division of M&I." M&I retains consent-free assignment routes.

elements.element: Customer's consent to Vendor assignment is not to be unreasonably withheld.
elements.evidence: Retained opening of 22.4 applies symmetrically: assignment requires "the prior written consent of the other party, which consent shall not be unreasonably withheld" — so any M&I assignment that does need consent is subject to the reasonableness standard.

elements.element: Vendor may never assign to a Customer competitor.
elements.evidence: No competitor bar exists in the rendered 22.4; nothing restricts the identity of M&I's assignee under proviso (b).

elements.element: Customer's change of control gives Vendor no termination right.
elements.evidence: Section 21.11.B: "If a Change in Control occurs with respect to Customer, M&I agrees to continue to provide Services under this Agreement", with the only qualifications being scope/volume limits (pre-change entities; prior 3-month volumes plus 25%) — no termination or re-pricing right for M&I.

elements.element: Both parties may assign to a successor.
elements.evidence: Customer: revised proviso (a) consent-free assignment "to a successor in a merger, acquisition or sale of all or substantially all of Customer's assets"; M&I: retained proviso (b)(i) free assignment on "merger, corporate reorganization or sale of all or substantially all of its assets, stock or securities".

elements.element: A successor assignment requires written notice.
elements.evidence: Added sentence: "The assigning party shall give the other party written notice of any assignment made under clause (a) or (b) above." This reaches both parties' consent-free successor assignments.

The opening consent requirement is retained ("may not be assigned by either party ... without the prior written consent of the other party"), but proviso (b)(ii) is left untouched and lets M&I freely assign "to any entity which is a successor to the assets or the business of the M&I Data Services division of M&I" — a consent-free transfer to a buyer of one M&I business unit while M&I itself survives, i.e. a retained non-successor (partial-business) exception. "Corporate reorganization" in (b)(i) is a further consent-free route that need not involve a successor to M&I. Under the ASSIGN fallback boundary, any retained no-consent non-successor exception defeats this element.

elements.element: Consent to other assignments is not to be unreasonably withheld.
elements.evidence: Retained: "which consent shall not be unreasonably withheld", applying mutually to all assignments outside the provisos.

reasons: Fallback is incomplete: "Other assignments require consent." fails because proviso (b)(ii) survives, giving M&I a consent-free right to assign to "any entity which is a successor to the assets or the business of the M&I Data Services division" — a divisional/partial-business transfer that is not a successor to the counterparty and therefore is an "other assignment" escaping the consent gate; the words "corporate reorganization" in (b)(i) create the same gap.

Repair in operative language: amend proviso (b) so M&I's consent-free right is limited to a successor to M&I by merger or sale of all or substantially all of its assets — i.e. delete "corporate reorganization" and delete clause (ii) (or make the divisional transfer subject to the prior-written-consent/not-unreasonably-withheld machinery). No other edits are needed to complete the fallback.

Preferred level fails on four elements (no Customer affiliate carve-out, M&I retains free assignment, no competitor bar), consistent with the drafter's decision not to pursue it; the change-of-control element and the reasonableness standard are already satisfied by retained text.

Minimality holds: the only substantive change is the scope of Customer's consent-free successor route (replacing the narrower $100,000,000 financial-institution merger test, which the new wording subsumes) plus the single mutual written-notice sentence required by the notice element; the Section 21.11 condition, the consent gate and the reasonableness standard are retained, and no extras (survival tails, procedures, expense language) are added.

Intent preserved: Section 21.11.B change-of-control mechanics, the Section 21.11 compliance condition and M&I's other commercial rights survive without contradiction; the notice sentence's reference to "clause (a) or (b)" tracks existing lettering and leaves no dangling cross-reference or undefined term.
